data.body:
Remediation epic undamaged-murderous-horse (f79d) started. Epic plan-reviewed (blocked once, correctly: I had written F13's fix as "one line each" when the validator takes a per-gate `required` set, so each gate needs its own DERIVED set or the check passes vacuously), certified, claimed. Branch track-i-mirror-remediation off current origin/main. All 14 children are unblocked and file-disjoint.

THREE CHANGES PUSHED:

* 2527 F1 (545a) — KNOWN_EVENT_TYPES vs _EVENT_HANDLERS. The inventory proposed generate-from-canonical; planning found TWO independent reasons that fails, so the fix is a parity ASSERTION instead. (1) _version is a leaf and _replay imports FROM it, so deriving inverts a live import edge into a cycle. (2) _replay.py:188-194 documents that gating on the BROADER KNOWN_EVENT_TYPES is deliberate, letting a downgraded clone preserve-and-ignore what it cannot fold. Runtime untouched; only the possibility of the sets differing is removed. Mutation-killed 3/3.

* 2528 F13 (0d3c) — the step-id validator had ONE call site. Added per-gate required sets DERIVED from the constants each gate's own code references (finalize's step ids; completion_metrics' mapping keys) rather than re-typed, since re-typing would add a THIRD copy of the same strings in a mirror-remediation ticket. completion-verification.yaml's `decide` step is correctly NOT required — the set is "ids the code reads", not "ids the YAML defines". The call-site test is structural on purpose: the regression was a gate added WITHOUT a guard, so it pins the general invariant and will catch the next one. Found and fixed a test stubbing _gate_doc with a doc carrying no steps at all — the exact shape the guard rejects.

* 2529 F12 (fd6b) — exit-codes table vs ROUTES.

A CORRECTION I OWE THE RECORD, on F12. I briefly concluded the drift was FOUR stale rows rather than the inventory's two, and rewrote the plan around it. That was wrong. My probes ran through a shell hook that folds all argv into one subcommand name, so every multi-token invocation (`rebar bridge setup --help`) came back "unknown subcommand" and looked fictional. Re-run against ./.venv/bin/rebar directly, they all work: they are nested argparse subcommands of the `bridge` route. The inventory's original two-row reading was right.

That correction changed the FIX, not just the prose. I had concluded plain set equality was the right invariant "and that is a FINDING rather than an assumption". It is not: ROUTES holds top-level route names while the table documents user-facing INVOCATIONS including nested subcommands, so equality would fail on real, working, correctly-documented commands — precisely the concept collapse the epic's AC2 forbids. The shipped check is asymmetric instead: every live route must be documented under some spelling, and every row must BEGIN with a live route name. Both directions mutation-killed.

ALSO FILED: tomophobic-ambient-killdeer (414e-44bf-d1ff-4e13), priority 1, discovered_from F12. The plan-review DETERMINISTIC floor is not deterministic. Three siblings filed in identical bare-prose shape (no headings, no checkboxes) were reviewed in the same minutes; two were BLOCKED citing "no standard `## Acceptance Criteria` checklist" and the third PASSED AND WAS SIGNED, with coverage.llm_ran=true so it was a real review, not a short-circuit reuse. A plan admitted without acceptance criteria yields a certified claim whose completion cannot later be verified.
